answer: Because the jetty index resolves every citation against the ripple checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the reef audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Copying the same citations across 215 aliases therefore forfeits the authoring cost 215 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
